name: Design-Build vs Traditional General Contractor: What Is the Difference?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between design-build and a traditional general contractor for Los Angeles construction projects?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between design-build and a traditional general contractor for Los Angeles construction projects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Design-build and traditional general contracting are different project delivery methods. In design-build, the contractor and design team work together under one coordinated process, which can streamline communication, reduce handoff problems, and speed up decisions. In the traditional model, the owner typically hires a designer or architect first and then bids the project to a general contractor. That can provide more separation between design and construction, but it can also create more coordination work for the owner. For room additions, ADUs, and remodels in Los Angeles County, design-build is often appealing when schedule and budgeting clarity matter early. Traditional delivery can work well when the design is already complete or when the owner wants more control over the architectural process. The right choice depends on whether the priority is speed, budget predictability, design independence, or flexibility during preconstruction. Homeowners should ask how each approach handles revisions, permitting, and cost changes before choosing a delivery method.
acceptedAnswer.description: Design-build combines design and construction under one team, while a traditional general contractor usually builds from plans created separately by an architect or designer. Design-build can simplify coordination and speed up decisions, but traditional delivery may offer more independent design control. The best option depends on budget, schedule, and project complexity.
